newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money traded at 8.0/9.0 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money traded at 8.0/9.0 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money was traded at 8.0/9.0 percent on Thursday morning on ample supply.
Dealers said operators were expecting a slightly tight market, but an ample market surprised many banks and caused overall rates to soften.
But they remained cautious because of the weekly tax payments due on Friday and a larger amount was expected to be due next Tuesday.
One- and three-month money were at 12.25/12.50 and 13.50/13.75 percent respectively.

The central bank was offering longer-term papers on Thursday. Bank Indonesia offered one-week SBIs at 6.5, two-week at 8.25 percent, one-month at 10.25 percent and three-month at 11.25 percent, six-month at 11.5 and one-year at 12.0 percent.
The average overnight interbank rate on Wednesday was 11.54 percent, compared with 11.91 percent on Tuesday.
Bond dealers said the secondary market was quiet, with focus on the primary market due to the approaching payment deadlines for many of the upcoming new issues.
"We are focusing more on the issues. But a softer market cause a slight decline in offer prices," one said.
